short: Conquered Wales, hammered Scotland, and turned Parliament into a habit.
full:
Edward was on crusade when his father Henry III died in 1272 and did not reach England until 1274. His first campaigns were in Wales: two wars, in 1277 and 1282-83, ended native rule under Llywelyn ap Gruffudd and were consolidated by the Statute of Rhuddlan and a ring of stone castles at Conwy, Caernarfon, Harlech and Beaumaris.

At home he legislated heavily, with statutes on land tenure, mortmain and merchants, and he summoned assemblies so often that Parliament became a fixture of royal government; the Model Parliament of 1295 included knights and burgesses alongside magnates. He expelled the Jewish community from England in 1290, after decades in which the crown had taxed it to exhaustion. From 1296 he intervened in the Scottish succession and then tried to conquer Scotland outright, a war he never finished. He died at Burgh by Sands in July 1307, marching north once more.
